opportunities.funder: Carnegie Trust for the Universities of Scotland
opportunities.title: Undergraduate Tuition Fee Grants

amount.raw: Our grants cover the cost of tuition fees, up to £1,820 per year for a full-time degree course.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Individuals from low-income households who are ordinarily resident in Scotland, enrolled on (or holding an unconditional offer for) an undergraduate degree course at an eligible Scottish institution, who are not eligible for government tuition fee support. Must be entitled to remain indefinitely in the UK or hold Limited Leave to Remain valid for the course, or be an asylum seeker.
opportunities.summary: Grants that cover undergraduate tuition fees (up to £1,820 per year) for students from low-income Scottish households who are ineligible for government tuition fee funding at Scottish higher education institutions. Includes a second-degree route for reskilling in skills-shortage subject areas.

opportunities.funder: Carnegie Trust for the Universities of Scotland
opportunities.title: Carnegie-Morgan Scholarship

amount.raw: Full tuition fees for the MSc in Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants plus an additional living-cost bursary of £1,200.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scottish-domiciled students from low-income households who have been accepted onto the MSc in Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants (delivered by Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh and University of Edinburgh), are ordinarily resident in Scotland with a meaningful connection, and have not already obtained a postgraduate degree.
opportunities.summary: A scholarship developed in partnership with the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh that funds full tuition fees and a £1,200 living-cost bursary for postgraduate study in plant science and botany (MSc Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants), aimed at widening participation and supporting Scotland's net-zero/biodiversity workforce. Applications are made after securing a place on the MSc course.
